subject: Request: Subprocessor roster, data flow, and transfer assurances
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finserve.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finserve.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Subprocessor roster, data flow, and transfer assurances

Hi Rishi,

Hope you’re well. As part of FinServe’s onboarding compliance review, we need a current list of Redwood’s subprocessors that may process FinServe data, plus any supporting materials that clarify how data flows to those subprocessors (network and storage boundaries). Specifically we’d like: 

- A CSV or spreadsheet with subprocessor name, country, role (e.g., CDN, telemetry, analytics), and whether they see plaintext data.
- A high-level data flow diagram (SVG/PDF) showing regional egress points and where encryption/in-transit protections apply.
- Confirmation of the contractual mechanism you rely on for EU data transfers (SCCs, BCRs, or adequacy) and whether any subprocessor is outside those protections.

We’re on a tight audit window and would appreciate these by EOD Thursday (20 Nov). If you anticipate any items that will be redacted for confidentiality, please call that out and provide a good-faith alternative (e.g., redacted vendor names + functional role).

Also flagged: our security team has a question about an observability vendor — do you use an external tracing/telemetry SaaS that receives spans or logs derived from customer request payloads? If yes, which vendor and what data is shipped?

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Vendor Risk Manager, FinServe

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finserve.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor roster, data flow, and transfer assurances

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. I’m looping in Neha (Legal) for contractual/transfer language and Maya (Infra) for the data flow/telemetry details. Laura (CS) will coordinate delivery to FinServe procurement and confirm timeline.

Quick answers so you have context:
- We’ll provide a CSV with the full roster; where confidentiality is required we’ll mark the entry and provide role-level detail.
- We maintain EU Standard Contractual Clauses for controller-processor transfers and also rely on adequacy for certain EU regions — Neha will confirm specifics and flag any exceptions.
- Observability: we use a telemetry pipeline that ships aggregated traces/metrics to a managed vendor for platform health; customer request payloads are not included in tracing exports by default. Maya will confirm exactly what fields are sent.

Target: preliminary roster + dataflow diagram by EOD Thu (20 Nov). If we need more time for redactions or third-party approvals we’ll call that out by Wed EOD.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20251118.csv (stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finserve.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor roster, data flow, and transfer assurances

Hi Oliver — Neha from Legal here. Per Rishi’s note:

1) Contractual transfer mechanism
We rely primarily on the EU Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses (processors-to-processor and controller-to-processor variants depending on the engagement). For customers in territories with adequacy decisions we rely on those where applicable. No BCRs at present. If your legal team requires alternate language, we can discuss a narrow DPA amendment.

2) Subprocessor disclosures / redactions
I’ve attached a redacted roster (attached CSV). Redaction rationale: we do not disclose fixed-price marketplace/connectors where disclosure risks supplier confidentiality; instead we provide role (e.g., "managed-cdn") and controls summary. If you need fully unredacted vendor names to complete your internal review we’ll route a limited-disclosure request under NDA — let us know.

3) DPA amendment / signature
I’ve drafted a short DPA amendment that clarifies transfer clauses and provides a 30-day notice requirement for subprocessor changes. Draft attached (dpa_amendment_draft.docx). If acceptable, we can route via DocuSign — link will be provided when we finalize edits.

4) Evidence and audit artifacts
We can produce SOC2 summary reports and a subprocessor compliance checklist for select vendors. Please indicate which artifacts you require for procurement acceptance.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_amendment_draft.docx

---
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finserve.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 11:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor roster, data flow, and transfer assurances

Hi Oliver — Maya from Infra. Quick technical notes to accompany the roster: 

- Data flows: attached PDF shows the egress points. Short summary: customer inference requests are terminated in-region; we persist model artifacts and telemetry in encrypted storage. Prefix/KV caches and some logs (masked) are routed to our analytics pipeline.
- Observability vendor: we use SkyTrace (managed SaaS) for aggregated platform metrics and non-sensitive traces. We DO NOT forward full customer request payloads to SkyTrace; traces include request IDs, timings, and anonymized model route information.
- CDN: we rely on a managed CDN partner in select regions for model shard distribution; the CDN caches only model artifacts and public static assets — not customer request or response bodies.

Attached: redwood_dataflow_v1.pdf (dataflow diagram) and the detailed CSV (redwood_subprocessors_20251118.csv) with role-level redactions indicated.

If you want a brief walk-through, happy to set a 30-min technical call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Maya
Director, Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dataflow_v1.pdf, redwood_subprocessors_20251118.csv

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finserve.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finserve.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor roster, data flow, and transfer assurances

Rishi / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. Procurement and InfoSec reviewed the CSV and diagram. A few follow-ups before we close the file: 

- Our legal team asked for the 30-day notice provision to be explicit in the executed DPA; the draft you shared looks good but Legal requests the DocuSign route and a named contact for change notifications.
- We need confirmation that CDN cache servers (the managed CDN you mentioned) will not hold any customer inference request/response payloads and that cache purges can be requested for our tenant if required.
- Could you confirm whether the SkyTrace deployment is multi-tenant (single instance serving multiple customers) vs. single-tenant projects per customer? That affects our risk assessment.

If those points are acceptable we can sign the amendment and move to procurement sign-off. Please:
1) Provide a DocuSign link for the amendment with notification contact filled in (or confirm who will be the contact).
2) Confirm the CDN/data retention answers in writing.

Appreciate it — Oliver
